entrypoints.summary: GET /examples returns example JSON records together with HMAC signatures computed over their signed fields.
POST /convert-to-yaml accepts a JSON data record and 64-character signature, derives signed data, selects an output prefix, and writes YAML.

affected_components.role: Derives signed data, authenticates own enumerable entries, consumes outputPrefix, and writes serialized YAML.
Relaunches the application after crash and later restores the backup.
Installs mutable app source, restart script, and setuid flag helper.

code_slices.fixed: No fixed code or patch is supplied.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The service obtains sample signed records from /examples; its denylist is applied to the output-file string before forming an /app-data/yamls path.
code_slices.vulnerable: getSignedData assigns signed.* suffixes into a normal object; getSignature uses Object.entries; the endpoint then reads signedData.outputPrefix and passes the constructed name to convertJsonToYaml and Bun.write.

negative_controls: No supplied execution result confirms the reverse-shell connection.
Ordinary conversion requests should not escape the configured YAML output directory.
observability.positive_marker: The conversion endpoint returns an output filename on success; the supplied solution expects a reverse-shell connection after the crash/restart sequence.

preconditions: The target is the supplied Bun/Hono Linux container with the mutable application source and restart loop.
The caller can reach GET /examples and POST /convert-to-yaml.
The runtime behavior for NUL-containing Bun paths and the referenced process descriptor must match the supplied challenge environment.

trigger_steps.summary: Fetch an example record and its valid signature from /examples.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Prototype-derived traversal/proc descriptor prefix with NUL plus key/value ordering that serializes as TypeScript.
trigger_steps.summary: Add signed.__proto__.outputPrefix targeting the process file descriptor and submit a YAML payload shaped as TypeScript.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: The official solution changes the inherited prefix to a proc descriptor path ending in an escaped character.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a second request intended to crash the Bun process so the supervisor starts the modified source.

capabilities.concept: arbitrary application-source overwrite through filesystem path confusion

impacts.concept: remote code execution in challenge container
protected flag disclosure through setuid helper

relation_candidates.rationale: The solution supplies signed.__proto__, and application code copies signed-prefixed fields into an ordinary object before reading outputPrefix.
The endpoint exposes signed examples and the solution reuses the returned signature while adding the prototype-derived outputPrefix.

relation_candidates.dst: arbitrary application-source overwrite through filesystem path confusion
relation_candidates.rationale: The endpoint interpolates outputPrefix into the Bun output path; the solution supplies a traversal/proc-fd/NUL prefix to target the running source descriptor.
The solution writes YAML intentionally shaped as TypeScript with Bun.spawnSync and then targets a crash; the runtime loop invokes bun run start repeatedly and restores only after five runs.
relation_candidates.src: arbitrary application-source overwrite through filesystem path confusion

relation_candidates.dst: remote code execution in challenge container
relation_candidates.rationale: The official solution constructs a reverse-shell command for the overwritten source.

relation_candidates.dst: protected flag disclosure through setuid helper
relation_candidates.rationale: The runtime image installs a setuid getflag helper, and its source switches to the flag owner UID and reads the protected flag file.
Rejecting prototype-affecting keys and consuming only own authenticated fields prevents inherited outputPrefix from determining the filename.
Canonical containment and safe no-follow creation under the output directory remove attacker-selected traversal/proc descriptor targets.
relation_candidates.src: arbitrary application-source overwrite through filesystem path confusion

relation_candidates.rationale: The supplied runtime executes mutable /app source in a restart loop; immutability and removal of the privileged helper are design-derived measures to prevent source replacement from becoming a privileged execution path.

impact.affected_asset: Mutable /app application source and the privileged setuid getflag/flag-read boundary in the challenge container.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote caller holding only a signature obtained from the public examples endpoint can attempt to select an unauthenticated output path, write YAML shaped as TypeScript, and trigger a restart.
impact.security_effect: Potential overwrite of the running TypeScript source followed by code execution after service restart; the supplied CTF solution targets a reverse shell.

causal_trace.summary: An unauthenticated client can obtain a signed example and submit a data record containing a signed.__proto__ property to the conversion endpoint.

getSignedData assigns the suffix of every signed.* key into a normal object, while getSignature hashes only Object.entries of that object. The solution uses signed.__proto__ to make outputPrefix inherited rather than an own signed entry, so the inherited value influences output selection without being included in the signed entry set.

The inherited outputPrefix is interpolated into a filename and passed to Bun.file/Bun.write after a substring denylist. The supplied solution sets it to a traversal path ending in /proc/self/fd/3 plus a NUL, intending the YAML write to overwrite the running application source descriptor.

The supplied solution shapes serialized YAML as TypeScript containing Bun.spawnSync, then sends a separate crash-inducing request; the restart loop relaunches the mutable application. The container also exposes a setuid helper that reads the protected flag file.

failure.operation: Bun.file/Bun.write on a filename derived from inherited outputPrefix

primary_invariant.statement: Every configuration value consumed to determine the output filename must be an own, authenticated signed field, and the resulting write must remain confined to a safely created file under the YAML output directory.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The service consumes inherited signedData.outputPrefix after authenticating only Object.entries(signedData), and constructs a Bun write path from that value with only substring denylist filtering.

quality.review_notes: Organizer source, runtime configuration, official writeup, and solution establish the intended CTF chain. No execution transcript is supplied, so the solution is an oracle/reproducer specification rather than evidence that execution succeeded. The writeup explicitly says the Bun crash behavior was stumbled upon and not fully understood; portability beyond the pinned Bun/Linux challenge runtime is uncertain. No upstream remediation patch or regression test is provided.

remediation.invariant_restored: Reject reserved/prototype-affecting signed keys; construct signed parameters with null-prototype own-property semantics; derive output names from an allowlisted token or enforce canonical containment and no-follow creation under the output directory; do not restart mutable code or expose a setuid flag reader to the service account.
mitigation_classes: canonical path containment with safe file creation
immutable application deployment and least privilege

oracle.channel: HTTP request sequence plus container flag helper
oracle.expected_negative: A request carrying signed.__proto__ or a path escaping the YAML directory should be rejected, while ordinary signed example conversion should write only a generated YAML file under the configured output directory.
oracle.expected_positive: The official solution's sequence obtains an example signature, submits the prototype-derived output prefix and TypeScript-shaped YAML payload, then submits a crash request intended to relaunch modified source and yield a reverse shell; a shell could invoke the setuid helper.
